prompt.adult: Hebrews 2:1 says we must give the more earnest heed to the things we have heard. Why?
prompt.child: Hebrews tells readers to pay close attention to the message they have heard. What reason does 2:1 give?
prompt.teen: Hebrews 2:1: “Therefore we must give the more earnest heed to the things we have heard,” why?
prompt.older: According to Hebrews 2:1, why must we give the more earnest heed to what we have heard?

verses.text: Therefore we must give the more earnest heed to the things we have heard, lest we drift away.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 1.
explanation.teen: 2:1 gives a command, then the reason for it. Read the reason.
explanation.older: It follows “the things we have heard,” in 2:1.

teaching.extended_explanation: 2:3 asks how we shall escape if we neglect so great a salvation, which was first spoken by the Lord.
teaching.takeaway: We must give earnest heed, lest we drift away.

prompt.adult: In 3:16-18 the writer asks a chain of questions about the people who left Egypt with Moses. To whom did He swear that they would not enter His rest?
prompt.child: Hebrews looks back at the people Moses led from Egypt. To whom did God swear that they would not enter His rest?
prompt.teen: Hebrews 3:18: “And to whom did He swear that they would not enter His rest, but to” whom?
prompt.older: According to Hebrews 3:18, to whom did He swear that they would not enter His rest?

choices.text: those who did not give thanks
those who did not keep the feasts
those who did not build altars

verses.text: For who, having heard, rebelled? Indeed, was it not all who came out of Egypt, led by Moses?
And to whom did He swear that they would not enter His rest, but to those who did not obey?

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 18.
explanation.teen: 3:16 asks who rebelled; 3:18 asks a second question and answers it in its last words. Read them.
explanation.older: It follows “that they would not enter His rest, but to” in 3:18.

teaching.extended_explanation: 3:16 says it was all who left Egypt, led by Moses. 3:19 adds that they could not enter in.
teaching.takeaway: He swore it to those who did not obey.

prompt.adult: 4:12 says God’s word is sharper than any two-edged sword. According to 4:13, nothing is hidden from His sight; to Him we must do what?
prompt.child: Hebrews says nothing is hidden from God’s sight. What does 4:13 say we must do before Him?
prompt.teen: Hebrews 4:13: “to the eyes of Him to whom we must” do what?
prompt.older: According to Hebrews 4:13, what must we do before Him from whose sight nothing is hidden?

verses.text: For the word of God is living and powerful, and sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing even to the division of soul and spirit, and of joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.
And there is no creature hidden from His sight, but all things are naked and open to the eyes of Him to whom we must give account.

explanation.child: Look at the very end of verse 13.
explanation.teen: 4:12 describes God’s word; 4:13 says nothing is hidden, then names Him by what we must do. Read the end.
explanation.older: It follows “to whom we must” in 4:13.

teaching.extended_explanation: 4:12 says the word is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart. 4:13 says there is no creature hidden from His sight.
teaching.takeaway: We must give account to Him.

prompt.adult: 13:2 says not to forget to entertain strangers. According to 13:3, how are they to remember the prisoners?
prompt.child: Hebrews tells believers to care about people in prison. How does 13:3 say to remember them?
prompt.teen: Hebrews 13:3: “Remember the prisoners as if” what?
prompt.older: According to Hebrews 13:3, how should believers remember the prisoners?

verses.text: Do not forget to entertain strangers, for by so doing some have unwittingly entertained angels.
Remember the prisoners as if chained with them—those who are mistreated—since you yourselves are in the body also.

explanation.adult: Read the words after “as if” in 13:3.
explanation.child: Look right after “as if” in verse 3.
explanation.teen: 13:2 is about strangers; 13:3 names the prisoners, then says how to remember them, before the dash. Read that part.
explanation.older: It follows “Remember the prisoners as if” in 13:3.

teaching.extended_explanation: 13:2 says some have unwittingly entertained angels. 13:3 also names those who are mistreated, since you yourselves are in the body also.
teaching.takeaway: Remember the prisoners as if chained with them.

prompt.adult: 12:9 compares human fathers who corrected us with the Father of spirits. According to 12:10, He chastens us for our profit, that we may be what?
prompt.child: Hebrews compares the discipline of human fathers with God’s discipline. What does 12:10 say God’s discipline is meant to make us?
prompt.teen: Hebrews 12:10: “but He for our profit, that we may be” what?
prompt.older: Following 12:9, what does 12:10 give as the purpose of the Father’s chastening?

verses.text: Furthermore, we have had human fathers who corrected us, and we paid them respect. Shall we not much more readily be in subjection to the Father of spirits and live?
For they indeed for a few days chastened us as seemed best to them, but He for our profit, that we may be partakers of His holiness.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 10.
explanation.teen: 12:9 asks a question about the Father of spirits; 12:10 contrasts the two kinds of fathers, then states His purpose. Read the end.
explanation.older: It follows “but He for our profit, that we may be” in 12:10.

teaching.extended_explanation: 12:9 asks whether we should not much more readily be in subjection to the Father of spirits and live. 12:10 says human fathers chastened for a few days as seemed best to them.
teaching.takeaway: He chastens us that we may be partakers of His holiness.

prompt.adult: Both 3:13 and 10:25 urge believers to exhort one another. According to 10:25, they should do so all the more as they see what?
prompt.child: Hebrews tells believers more than once to encourage one another. In 10:25, what should make them do it even more?
prompt.teen: Hebrews 10:25: “and so much the more as you see” what?
prompt.older: Alongside 3:13, what does 10:25 say believers will see that should spur them to exhort one another more?

verses.text: but exhort one another daily, while it is called “Today,” lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin.
And let us consider one another in order to stir up love and good works,
not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as is the manner of some, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching.

explanation.child: Look at the very end of verse 25.
explanation.teen: 3:13 says to exhort one another daily; 10:25 says not to forsake meeting together, then gives a reason for doing it more. Read the end.
explanation.older: It follows “so much the more as you see” in 10:25.

teaching.extended_explanation: 3:13 warns against being hardened through the deceitfulness of sin. 10:24 says to consider one another in order to stir up love and good works.
teaching.takeaway: Exhort one another all the more as you see the Day approaching.

prompt.adult: 10:36 says they have need of endurance after doing the will of God. In 6:12, what do those who through faith and patience do?
prompt.child: Hebrews urges readers not to become lazy, but to copy people of faith and patience. What do those people do, according to 6:12?
prompt.teen: Hebrews 6:12: “imitate those who through faith and patience” do what?
prompt.older: With 10:36 in view, what does 6:12 say those who through faith and patience do?

verses.text: that you do not become sluggish, but imitate those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
For you have need of endurance, so that after you have done the will of God, you may receive the promise:

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 12.
explanation.teen: 10:36 is about endurance; 6:12 warns against being sluggish, then names whom to imitate and what they do. Read the end.
explanation.older: It follows “imitate those who through faith and patience” in 6:12.

teaching.extended_explanation: 6:11 asks each one to show the same diligence to the full assurance of hope. 6:12 warns them not to become sluggish.
teaching.takeaway: Those who through faith and patience inherit the promises.

prompt.adult: 10:35 says not to cast away your confidence, which has great reward. According to 3:14, we share in Christ if we hold the beginning of our confidence how?
prompt.child: Hebrews tells readers not to let go of their confidence. In 3:14, how must they hold the confidence they had at the beginning?
prompt.teen: Hebrews 3:14: “if we hold the beginning of our confidence” how?
prompt.older: Alongside 10:35, how does 3:14 say we must hold the beginning of our confidence?

verses.text: For we have become partakers of Christ if we hold the beginning of our confidence steadfast to the end,
Therefore do not cast away your confidence, which has great reward.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 14.
explanation.teen: 10:35 warns against casting confidence away; 3:14 states a condition about holding it. Read the end of that condition.
explanation.older: It follows “the beginning of our confidence” in 3:14.

teaching.extended_explanation: 10:35 says that confidence has great reward. 10:36 adds that they have need of endurance.
teaching.takeaway: Hold the beginning of our confidence steadfast to the end.
